newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends lower despite Iraq, API's awaited.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends lower despite Iraq, API's awaited.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil and refined product prices ended lower after getting a lift earlier in the afternoon on news suggesting Iraqi oil sales were being delayed, traders said Tuesday.
Gasoline's weakness was weighing on the market amid continued talk about upcoming voluminous imports, plus disappointing demand, traders said.

October crude settled six cents lower at $21.56 a barrel, shaking off a bullish rise in the early afternoon on comments a top Iraqi official at the UN that the U.S. was hindering the implementation of the May 20, UN-Iraq oil for food deal.
But a UN spokeswoman denied the allegations, and oil markets never seemed too interested in the news anyway.
September gasoline closed 0.41 cent lower at 61.21 cents amid the talk as many as 13 cargoes of conventional and reformulated gasoline would arrive on the East Coast by the first week of September.
Cash differentials in New York Harbor eased a bit on the talk, adding credence to the talk on the NYMEX, traders said.
Heating oil, resisting the drop, eeked out a 0.10 cent gain, settling at 61.13 cents a gallon, amid continued views stocks are bullishly low for late August.
On the inventory front, traders were expecting crude and distillate stocks to rise, gasoline stocks to fall and runs to remain about unchanged.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
